AC_findings.title: A03 exact Gevrey native integer drive and logarithmic-squared cofactor reduction
AC_findings.locator: Integrated §§2,4,9; Proof record6 pp28-31, esp Theorem A3-G2 and equations3.4,4.2,5.1
exact_content: r=1/4096; c_j=r/[j(j+1)]; q_r is the literal infinite uniform convolution; k_r=q_r_second-q_r/4; h=k_r*k_r, d=2r=1/2048. This is the historical two-copy source, distinct from Round2 jPlus.
N=sum n^(-1/2)delta_log(n), M=sum mu(n)n^(-1/2)delta_log(n), Pi=sum Lambda(n)n^(-1/2)delta_log(n); U=(tN)*h; F=Pi*h=M*U; N*F=U locally.
The source is Gevrey2; exact Poisson zero mode cancels by K(1/2)=K_prime(1/2)=0; |U(t)|<=C exp(-kappa exp(t/2)) for t>=0. Constants are source-dependent, no numerical kappa supplied.
For one fixed B with kappa*sqrt(B)>1/2, Fsmall_B(t)=sum_(n<=e^t/(B*t^2))mu(n)n^(-1/2)U(t-log n) satisfies |Fsmall_B(t)|<=2C/(sqrt(B)*t)*exp(-(kappa sqrt(B)-1/2)t).

F(t)=S_B(t)+Fsmall_B(t), with S_B=sum_(2<=m<B exp(d)t^2)(log m)/sqrt(m) sum_(n>e^t/(B t^2), mn<=e^(t+d)) mu(n)/sqrt(n) h(t-log(mn)). Both sums are finite. The sharp time-dependent threshold and full cross terms are load-bearing.
Alternate cutoff e^t/t^(2+eta), eta>0, gives independently superexponential small-divisor decay; one fixed B is not claimed to give every arbitrary decay rate.

exact_content: For X=e^(t+d), Y=e^t/(B t^2), define A_Y(k)=sum_(n|k,n>Y)mu(n)log(k/n). Then S_B=sum_(k<=X)A_Y(k)/sqrt(k)h(t-log k).

Eventually Y>sqrt(X), and every active prime-power coefficient A_Y(p^j)=0, including repeated powers. This is exact cancellation after smoothing, not permission to delete prime powers from the original source.
If q>Y prime, qm<=X, then A_Y(qm)=-Lambda(m); in particular A_Y(2q)=-log2. If p,q<=Y<pq and p^2q<=X, p!=q, then A_Y(p^2q)=log p>0.
Ordinary fixed-ratio PNT places both signs in every sufficiently late fixed open source interval on which h has one sign. No short-interval uniformity theorem or sampled detector value is claimed.

The full energy is the finite double-cofactor/divisor Gram sum with genuine mu(n)mu(k), time-dependent n>Y(t),k>Y(t) INSIDE its integral, all pairs m,ell and source overlaps. Nonnegativity of this Gram supplies no upper.
controls: Replacing mu by mu^2 preserves the same source/cutoff removal while the actual-input control grows like P_r(i/2)^2 exp(t/2)/zeta(2). Magnitudes and short cofactor count alone cannot close.
A hypothetical multiplicity-m zero leaves nonzero residue -mK(lambda); exact Gevrey shortening retains it. Do not infer a pointwise explicit decomposition of the atomic Mobius measure.
